title: Baseline ladder — skill measured against do-nothing rules, and what luck could explain

assumed_price_block.why_assumed: No official NFL source publishes a price for any market (probe P5/P6/P12). A standard -110 is therefore imposed as a stated assumption so that hit rate can be compared with the rate required to break even. It is not a quote, not a recommendation, and not evidence about any real sportsbook.
assumed_price_block.push_note: pushes are excluded from the denominator and returned, not counted as wins

findings.best_spread_rule_label: Recent form — last 5 games, points for/against + home edge
findings.how_to_read: An arm is not a signal because its ROI is positive. It is a signal only if its hit-rate confidence interval clears the break-even rate. At these sample sizes almost nothing can clear it, and that is the finding.

caveats: Every strategy here was selected from a family of 12 after the fact; a family-wise correction is required before any of it can be called a discovery (origination gate G5).
The assumed -110 ignores pushes correctly at the bet level but ignores vig on pushes, line movement, limits and availability. It is a hurdle, not a simulation of a book.
Week 10 finals did not exist at capture time (probe P11), so none of this is graded on the current slate.
B05 uses future games on purpose. It is published as a leakage ceiling and is excluded from every 'best rule' and 'profitable' computation.
